title: Sensor tags as rows
prompt: The facilities dashboard filters readings by placement tag, so it needs one row per tag. Write `solve(sensor_readings)` with `mapInPandas` so it returns `reading_id`, `device_id` and `tag`, one row for each tag of each reading.
rules: A reading with three tags gives three rows. A reading with an empty or missing tag list gives no rows.
Keep every delivered row: a reading delivered twice gives its tag rows twice.
Make the tag rows with `mapInPandas`: the check looks for it in the plan Spark runs.
Return `reading_id`, `device_id` and `tag`, all text, in that order.
hints: The starter already pulls the tag list out of `payload` into a `tags` column. Each value arrives in pandas as an array.
pandas' `explode("tags")` gives one row per list element. An empty or missing list becomes a single row with a missing value; drop those with `dropna`.
Don't remove duplicates inside the function: the rules keep every delivery.
starter:
import pandas as pd
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(sensor_readings):
    # The tag list from inside the payload struct, as a plain column.
    readings = sensor_readings.select("reading_id", "device_id", F.col("payload.tags").alias("tags"))
    # Return one row per tag: reading_id, device_id, tag.
    return readings
